title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Replacing one Co2+ of a Co4 cubane water-oxidation catalyst by a redox-inert Ln3+ gives an LnCo3 cubane that both mimics the Ca site of the natural OEC and uses flexible water/acetate ligands to improve photocatalytic water oxidation.
explanation: LnCo3 (Ln = Ho–Yb) reached TON 211 and TOF 9 s−1, versus 40 and 5 s−1 for the earlier Co-only WOC. UV–vis, HPLC, and solution XAS supported catalyst integrity, and Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics plus later computations linked activity to ligand flexibility around Ln3+.
scope: 3d–4f cubane [LnCo3(hmp)(OAc)] water-oxidation catalysts derived from the Co4 hmp cubane.
conditions: 470 nm irradiation, [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2, Na2S2O8, water; ErCo3 is the Table 1 entry.
caveats: Mn cubanes inspired by {CaMn4O5} are described as often unstable, which is why Co/Ni/Cu–Ln cubanes were pursued; the numerical gain is relative to one prior Co4 catalyst.
